poincare_wirtinger.type: theorem poincare_wirtinger (hab : a < b) {f f' : R -> C} (hderiv : forall x, x in [[a, b]] -> HasDerivAt f (f' x) x) (hper : f b = f a) (hmean : fourierCoeffOn hab f 0 = 0) (hintf' : IntervalIntegrable f' volume a b) (hL2f : MemLp f 2 (volume.restrict (Ioc a b))) (hL2f' : MemLp f' 2 (volume.restrict (Ioc a b))) : (integral over [a,b] of ||f||^2) <= ((b - a) / (2 * pi))^2 * (integral over [a,b] of ||f'||^2)
poincare_wirtinger.justification: hderiv: C^1 regularity on the closed interval, used by fourierCoeffOn_of_hasDerivAt (integration by parts); hper: endpoint matching is exactly the descent condition to the circle R/(b-a)Z, kills the boundary term; hmean: mean zero in the torus normalization (zero-th Fourier coefficient), kills the n = 0 mode; hintf'/hL2f/hL2f': standard integrability requirements for Parseval applied to f and f'. All six are discharged by sine_wave_hypotheses for the sine wave.
poincare_wirtinger.constant: ((b-a)/(2*pi))^2 = reciprocal of the first nonzero Laplacian eigenvalue of the circle; optimality proved in poincare_constant_sharp
poincare_wirtinger.norm: L^2 on the interval, the standard L^2 norm of the circle

heat_evolve.type: theorem heatSeries_hasSum (T) [Fact (0 < T)] (t : NNReal) (f : Lp C 2 haarAddCircle) : HasSum (fun n : Z => (heatWeight T t n : C) *s (fourierCoeff f n *s fourierLp 2 n)) (heatEvolve T t f); theorem heatEvolve_tendsto_self (f) : Tendsto (fun t : NNReal => heatEvolve T t f) (nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0)) (nhds f); theorem heatEvolve_add (s t) : heatEvolve T s (heatEvolve T t f) = heatEvolve T (s + t) f
heat_evolve.justification: L^2 w.r.t. the probability Haar measure on AddCircle T; the series is the full infinite sum over Z; convergence from Parseval (hasSum_sq_fourierCoeff) via ell^2 summability; the t -> 0+ limit via Tannery's theorem dominated by the Parseval-summable sequence n |-> ||c_n(f)||^2
heat_evolve.constants: eigenvalues lambda_n = (2 pi n / T)^2; weights exp(-lambda_n t)
heat_evolve.norm: L^2 norm of the probability Haar measure

D12-comparison-geodesics: JacobiSolutionOn carries explicit pointwise HasDerivAtR derivative data du, ddu and C¹-on-[a,b] continuity; the ODE is u'' + k·u = 0 on the open interval with the curvature inequality k₂ ≤ k₁ on the closed interval — no smoothness of k is assumed anywhere.

Riccati comparisons require positivity of the solutions u₁, u₂ on the closed interval Icc a b (not merely the open one); this is exactly what makes every denominator bounded away from zero and is the standard no-conjugate-point hypothesis on the finite interval.

The singular Riccati comparisons require continuity of m, m̄ on Ioc 0 T = (0,T] (v2 corrected domain) — continuity on [0,T] would contradict the Euclidean normalization (proved: euclideanNormalizedOn_not_continuousOn_zero). The initial conditions are the quantitative Euclidean normalization |m t − d/t| ≤ C, |m̄ t − d/t| ≤ C on (0,t₀]; for a Jacobi field with u 0 = 0, u' 0 = 1 and bounded u'' this normalization is derivable (documented as the missing bridge lemma; the honest u(0)=0, u'(0)=1 form is the expanded-hypothesis target for the Rauch corollary).

The volume-ratio chain requires: A, Ā C¹ on (0,T) with m = A'/A, m̄ = Ā'/Ā pointwise; A, Ā > 0 on (0,T] (positivity on the correct half-open interval); A, Ā continuous on [0,T]; A 0 = Ā 0 = 0 (areas of the radius-0 sphere); d > 0; 0 < t₀ ≤ T; C ≥ 0; k̄ ≤ k on (0,T). Each hypothesis is exactly the analytic image of a standard Bishop-Gromov hypothesis; none is equivalent to the conclusion (the Euclidean model satisfies all of them and the conclusion is not trivially forced for non-model data).
Non-vacuity is witnessed by the Euclidean model m = d/t, A = t^d with k = k̄ = 0, C = 0 (ModelEuclidean.lean), including the explicit volume V t = t^(d+1)/(d+1).
